transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-03
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Liam Chen (Redwood SE); Carlos Mendez (CTO, Hemera); Priya Rao (Platform Eng); Sofia Kim (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery call. Hemera exploring Redwood for inference for their documentation assistant and search ranking microservice. Main concerns: latency SLOs, cost at scale, and data residency/compliance for EU customers. Interested in fast time-to-first-token via quickstart credits but may need Dedicated or Private for production.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I think we scheduled 40 minutes, so we'll try to be efficient. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the PLG motion, and Liam from our infra SE team is here to dive into any technical bits.
00:18 Carlos: Hi Maya, hi Liam. Carlos here. CTO at Hemera. We run a mix of SaaS and on-prem connectors for enterprise customers.
00:25 Priya: Priya, platform eng. I own our infra and networking for the services we'll be putting LLMs behind.
00:30 Sofia: Sofia, product — evaluating UX and success criteria.
00:34 Liam (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Quick agenda — understand your current stack and constraints, run through hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private), talk TTFT — time-to-first-token — and then next steps.
00:45 Carlos: Sounds good. Our timeline's pretty tight. We want a prototype internal demo for the execs in three weeks. Ideally two weeks to see something.
00:52 Maya: That's achievable, that's exactly what the quickstart credits and self-serve flow are for. We'll map the production conversation after the pilot.
01:02 Sofia: Two things up front — latency expectations and data residency. Most of our customers in EU need EU-only processing.
01:12 Priya: Also encryption at rest + KMS integration, and we need audit logs for data handling.
01:18 Maya: Totally. We support hosted with region selection, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For EU residency, hosted EU regions can often work for pilots; Private is for strict controls.
01:28 Carlos: For pilot can we do EU-hosted? We want to hit a demo with EU data.
01:34 Liam: Yes, we have EU regions. Note that network latency can bite if your service layer is outside the region, but for the quick sprint we can provision EU-hosted instances.
01:46 Maya: Quick question on workloads — what are the request patterns? Spiky? Short prompts? Batch?
01:52 Carlos: Mostly short prompts, 30-120 tokens typical, bursty during business hours. Expected qps maybe 30-100 for the demo. Production could be higher.
02:04 Priya: And we want p95 latency under 200ms for those short prompts. 200ms p95 is our goal.
02:12 Liam: Good to know. For short prompts at that QPS, hosted will usually meet the latency if routed to EU region and using a smaller model variant. Dedicated gives more predictable latency if you need firm SLOs. Private is more about isolation and compliance.
02:28 Maya: On the credits: we can allocate free quickstart credits to run the two-week pilot and cover a baseline of tokens plus some dedicated benchmarking slots to run p95 tests.
02:38 Carlos: How long to spin up Dedicated? We need to estimate lead time if we end up needing it.
02:45 Liam: Dedicated provisioning typically is a few business days if capacity is available; with committed contracts it's faster. Private on-prem takes more — that's usually 4-8 weeks depending on network setup and any air-gapped requirements.
02:58 Sofia: And what about costs for the pilot vs production? We don't want surprises when scaling.
03:04 Maya: We'll send a pricing sheet with example unit economics. Typically hosted is pay-as-you-go so you can run the pilot cheaply. Dedicated gives better cost predictability per throughput. There's also our Optimize toolkit for batching and quantization recommendations.
03:21 Priya: Do you guys have a recommended model for a doc-assistant use case? We want quality similar to gpt-like responses but cheaper.
03:30 Liam: For doc assistant, a medium-sized open model often balances quality and cost. We also offer quantized variants that reduce GPU cost. For ranking/embedding calls we can use smaller specialized models.
03:42 Carlos: Can we test model variants easily during the pilot? We want to compare latency/cost across 2-3 models.
03:48 Liam: Yes, our platform supports quick switching and routing policies. For the pilot we'll set up A/B routes so you can compare.
03:55 Speaker 1 (customer, unclear): mm-hmm, okay.
04:02 Priya: On the security front — do you support customer-managed keys? We use AWS KMS and have HSM requirements for some customers.
04:09 Maya: Yes, KMS integrations are supported in Private and in Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted, we have options for bring-your-own-key in certain enterprise plans. We'll share the security docs.
04:21 Carlos: SOC2? ISO? Any certifications?
04:24 Liam: We have SOC 2 Type II. ISO is in progress — we'll share the certificate and the typical architecture diagrams that auditors ask for.
04:33 Sofia: Great. Let's talk TTFT — for a quick PoC, how quickly can we go from sign-up to first successful inference?
04:41 Maya: For self-serve hosted, median time-to-first-token for teams who follow the quickstart is under 2 hours — including API key issuance, sample app run, and a basic prompt. With our free credits applied, you basically can run the sample and do a few calls.
04:55 Carlos: Two hours? That seems optimistic. What's usually the blocker?
04:59 Maya: Usually onboarding payment or corporate firewall rules if they block outbound calls. Also sometimes teams need to wire up the SDK into their app.
05:07 Priya: For us firewall egress to EU endpoints is allowed, so should be fine. We do have strict IP allowlist rules for production.
05:15 Liam: For production we can support IP allowlists and VPC peering for Dedicated/Private. We'll capture the network requirements in the infra checklist.
05:24 Sofia: For the demo, we want to show a search over docs and a short chat demo — about 2-3 flows. Are there templates?
05:31 Maya: Yes we have quickstart templates and sample apps. We can provision a repo, or share a live demo link.
05:36 Priya: Could you send us the repo link and a runbook for the demo?
05:39 Maya: Absolutely, Liam will share the runbook.
05:42 Liam: I'll add a checklist: env vars, API key steps, region selection, example prompt sets for latency measurement, and k6 scripts if you want to simulate QPS.
05:54 Carlos: On data handling — we have customer PII in some docs. Do you offer automatic redaction or data masking?
06:02 Liam: We have built-in redaction helpers and an audit log. For hosted flows you can enable redaction or use policy-based filtering; for Private you can run your own preprocessor before forwarding to the model. Our logs can be configured to mask tokens.
06:17 Sofia: Will that affect latency?
06:20 Liam: Minimal, depends on whether you preprocess client-side or inline. We recommend client-side preprocessing when latency is critical.
06:27 Priya: For the pilot should we send sample PII or redacted examples?
06:31 Carlos: We'll redact before sending. We'll also share a few representative prompts.
06:35 Maya: Perfect. That'll help with recommending the model/quantization settings.
06:40 Speaker 2 (Redwood): um so for SLA — what uptime targets are you expecting?
06:45 Carlos: We're not at the SLA negotiation yet, but want to understand availability and what guarantees look like for Dedicated.
06:51 Liam: Dedicated comes with an SLA; hosted has best-effort but we have regional fallbacks. For hard enterprise contracts we'll put numbers in the sample SLA.
06:59 Priya: Are you able to do canary rollouts and A/B model rollbacks? We want automatic fallback if a model variant is degraded.
07:07 Liam: Yes, rollouts and automatic fallback are supported. You can set routing policies that fall back to a cheaper or earlier model if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds.
07:16 Sofia: Ok good. Let's talk numbers for the pilot credits. How many tokens should we ask for to cover the benchmark?
07:22 Maya: If you run simulated bursts and manual testing, I'd suggest 5M tokens to be comfortable for a two-week pilot. We can tailor based on expected prompt lengths and QPS.
07:31 Carlos: 5M seems okay. Please include examples of token burn by scenario so execs know the cost.
07:37 Maya: Will do.
07:39 Priya: On EU-hosted — what's the latency we'd expect for a 50ms compute time model? Our app is in EU-West.
07:47 Liam: Network hops add some overhead. From EU-West to the region and back, you'd see maybe 20-50ms added depending on routing. Combine that with model compute and you're in the 100-200ms ballpark for short prompts.
07:59 Carlos: That's borderline but might be acceptable for the demo. For prod we might need Dedicated pinned in the same region.
08:07 Maya: Makes sense. For the pilot we can start hosted EU region and if we see jitter we can spin a Dedicated pool.
08:14 Speaker 1 (customer): okay yeah
08:20 Sofia: Are there any compliance questionnaires you usually get from customers? We have a security review in two weeks.
08:25 Liam: We commonly provide a security pack — SOC2 report, architecture, encryption docs, and a dataflow diagram. We'll put together a customer-ready packet.
08:34 Carlos: Great — can you email that by EOD Friday?
08:37 Maya: We'll aim for Friday EOD.
08:40 Priya: Demo infra question — can we run our benchmarking script against a staging endpoint or will we need credentials per user?
08:47 Liam: We'll create API keys scoped to the pilot and you can hit the staging/test endpoints. We'll also give a sandbox region so it won't affect production capacity.
08:56 Carlos: For the A/B routing — how do you measure quality differences? Do you provide eval tooling?
09:02 Liam: We have an Optimize toolkit that can run eval sets and surface quality regressions tied to prompts. For the pilot we'll help you run an eval against a small test set.
09:12 Sofia: Good. Ok a more practical question — SDK language support? We use Node for front end and Go for the backend microservices.
09:19 Maya: Official SDKs for Node and Python; we also have an HTTP REST API and community Go client examples. For microservices calling from Go, REST is straightforward.
09:28 Priya: Any rate limiting or concurrency limits we should plan for?
09:32 Liam: For hosted, there's soft rate limits per account but we can bump for the pilot. Dedicated is sized to your throughput. We'll include the default limits in the runbook.
09:41 Carlos: What about model KV cache — do you maintain persistent KV cache for longer conversations? We have sessioned flows.
09:48 Liam: We support KV cache management. For long conversations we suggest a hybrid approach: local session window + KV cache for longer context. Note that keeping large KV caches increases memory footprint and might affect latency.
09:59 Maya: Quick recap — we'll apply quickstart credits to Hemera, Liam will send the runbook and infra checklist, and we'll provide security docs and a pricing + token burn sheet. You'll provision EU-hosted for the pilot and we'll measure p95 latency against your criteria.
10:15 Carlos: Sounds good. Can we get a proposed kickoff slot for Monday?
10:19 Maya: I'll propose Monday and another optional Tuesday slot after the call.
10:23 Sofia: One last thing — any talk about on-prem agent install? Some of our enterprise customers demand air-gapped.
10:30 Liam: On-prem package exists but it's more involved — typically 4-8 weeks including networking and cert exchange. We can discuss later if pilot indicates that direction.
10:39 Priya: Fine for now. We'll proceed with hosted EU pilot.
10:42 Maya: Ok I'll follow up with an email with the links, docs, and proposed times. Thanks everyone.
10:49 Carlos: Thanks, appreciate it.
10:52 Sofia: Thanks.
10:54 End of call.

Notes on transcription: some words like "KV cache" were transcribed as "K V cash" in a few places; speaker labels may show "Speaker 1/2" where attendee audio overlapped.
